title: Relocation-transparent cross-Module references
statement: Cross-Module semantic references MUST be relocation-transparent and MUST NOT encode provider physical location where a supported stable identity or native package surface exists.
rationale: Stable identities preserve architectural meaning through physical restructuring while an explicit resolution boundary concentrates the unavoidable mapping from meaning to current repository location.
failure_prevented: Repository-wide path churn, stale navigation, machine-specific authority, direct source traversal across Module boundaries, and accidental conversion of a physical move into semantic delete-and-recreate work.
applicability: Every understood reference-bearing governed artifact in a repository using recursive Fortress Modules.
evaluation: Reference Resolution consumes the canonical CCG and exact snapshot bytes, resolves stable Module identities to canonical repository-relative paths, structurally inventories Cargo and Rust path boundaries, reconciles Markdown projections, and rejects understood machine-local or unregistered cross-Module physical coupling.

finding.message: An understood governed reference persists machine-local location, crosses a Module through unregistered physical traversal, or disagrees with its stable identity's current CCG projection.

remediation: Replace cross-Module physical coupling with the target's stable Fortress identity or native package surface, keep unavoidable paths inside a registered resolution boundary, and regenerate derived navigation from the current CCG.
valid_example: A contract requires CAP-FOO from AF-FOO-0001, Rust imports the stable crate surface, Cargo alone maps that crate to its current path, and README navigation is regenerated from AF-FOO-0001 after a move.
invalid_example: A contract or ordinary source file names ../../../mods/foo, a README relationship points to the old Module path, or a governed reference persists C:\Users\name\repo\mods\foo.
exception_policy: Same-Module relative references and registered path-only resolution boundaries remain valid; cross-Module physical coupling outside those exact semantics has no local exemption.
history: Introduced to make stable Module identity authoritative across physical relocation and to bound unavoidable path churn.
